what_it_does: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are AI models that operate on graph-structured data — social networks, molecular structures, recommendation systems — where the connections between items matter as much as the items themselves. Running them efficiently is hard because graphs are irregular: one node may have three neighbors and another may have three thousand, so memory is accessed in unpredictable scattered patterns that GPUs handle poorly. One performance trick is to reorder or merge operations (algebraic transformations), but the best reordering depends on the shape of the specific graph being processed, which changes every time the model sees a new input. Voyager solves this by choosing and combining transformations at runtime after looking at quick statistics about the current graph (for example, how spread-out the number of connections is), then generating an optimized execution plan tailored to that particular input — rather than compiling one fixed plan that is mediocre for every graph.
